source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Clear BMC SEL & OS event logs before test starts.
2. Power on SUT by press power button then boot into OS.
3. Clear BMC log and system event log under OS.
4. Copy BurnInTest tool to OS,
5. Select CPU/Memory/HDD to run and start to stress over (48hrs).
6. Check CPU/Memory is full loading in Task manager->Performance page

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. BurnIn test log/BMC log/System log no error info.
2. No system hang or blue screen happened.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Generic sustained fio/badblocks stress against RAID VD.
deepseek_columns.risk: 48-hour sustained I/O; cooling and approval required.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; notes duration and storage risk but substitutes storage-only fio/badblocks for BurnInTest CPU, memory, HDD and Windows evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; preserves BurnInTest coverage, baseline logs, target safety, watchdogs, OOB recovery and 172800-second duration.

original_test_intent: Run the specified Windows BurnInTest CPU, memory and HDD workload continuously for more than 48 hours, verify full CPU/memory load, and demonstrate no BurnInTest, BMC or system errors, hang or blue screen.
original_method: A person performs the source's physical power-button start and confirms the Task Manager Performance view; the agent stages the approved BurnInTest build/profile, runs the unchanged 48-hour plan, continuously monitors workload/thermal/storage/OS/BMC state, and retains baseline and delta logs rather than destroying evidence.
manual_activity: The source explicitly requires pressing the physical power button and inspecting Task Manager's Performance page. After those operator actions establish/confirm the environment, the 48-hour core workload, continuous monitoring and evidence collection can run automatically.
required_inputs: BurnInTest edition/version/license, executable hash and exact CPU/memory/HDD profile
Serial-bound disposable or explicitly writable storage target and capacity limits
Required load thresholds and sampling cadence for CPU/memory/HDD
172800+ second duration, start/end policy and one-user approval
Thermal/power/ECC/controller/OS stop thresholds and OOB recovery
Known-event allowlist and reviewed referenced-script revision
safety_requirements: Archive baseline BMC SEL and Windows event logs before any source-requested clear; never erase the only evidence.
Do not write-stress boot, mounted production, protected, customer or unidentified storage.
Validate cooling, power, OOB reachability and automated safety-stop thresholds before start.
Stop on thermal/power limits, uncorrectable ECC, controller reset, filesystem/storage error, hang or blue screen.
Do not automatically resume or retry after interruption; preserve the first-failure timeline.
agent_execution_scope: Verify tool/profile/script integrity and target/load/watchdog/recovery gates.
Start the approved unchanged 48-hour BurnInTest plan after operator setup and collect utilization/health telemetry throughout.
Detect reachability, hang/bugcheck, controller/storage, thermal, ECC and BMC events with explicit safety stops.
Collect final BurnInTest and system evidence, compare known events and report Tool Result without verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the complete 48-hour plan and perform the specified power-button start.
Confirm the Task Manager CPU/memory full-load view and any required photos.
Evaluate errors/exceptions and issue PASS/FAIL; authorize recovery if stopped.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not equivalent: fio/badblocks alone omits the named BurnInTest tool, CPU and memory workloads, Task Manager check, Windows system logs and blue-screen criterion; badblocks may be destructive.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the source-linked BurnInTest project script only after review, with the approved BurnInTest profile and independent read-only monitoring; fio may supplement HDD coverage only if formally approved.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU/Memory/HDD selection, over 48 hours (machine time 2880 minutes), Task Manager check and 30-minute attended field are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Pin the BurnInTest profile and script, preserve pre-clear log snapshots, stream utilization and platform telemetry, and produce a gap-aware 48-hour timeline with explicit safety stops.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Approved Windows build, RAID target and server thermal/power design.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BurnInTest/script, Windows, driver, controller/firmware and BMC versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BurnInTest vendor documentation, platform thermal limits and referenced project script.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds reproducibility and continuous safety evidence; it does not replace BurnInTest or manual Task Manager observation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Named workload profile and safety envelope.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A 48-hour exit code is insufficient if monitoring has gaps or the storage target was wrong.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve different load percentages or duration, but the report must state the override and cannot claim completion of the original over-48-hour plan if shortened.
expected_evidence: Hardware/firmware/storage pre-state, archived baseline logs, tool/script hashes and approval
Operator power-button and Task Manager full-load evidence
Complete 48-hour workload configuration/timeline plus CPU/memory/HDD, thermal, power, ECC and controller telemetry
BurnInTest result, Windows/BMC log deltas, no-hang/bugcheck evidence, final health, Tool Result and verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criteria consistently describe BurnInTest stress and error/hang absence. Repeated log clearing is unsafe evidence handling but not a contradictory test objective; archived baselines preserve intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Tool/profile, target and thresholds are project readiness inputs. The intended burn-in is clear and executable after they are approved.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects the fio/badblocks replacement as a coverage loss while retaining its long-duration/cooling caution.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its governed hybrid plan and identifies the manual source actions that justify the partial class.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates preserved baseline, automated execution status, safety stop, Tool Result and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Keeps CPU, memory, HDD, Windows UI and no-blue-screen coverage intact while making the long run auditable and safe.
independent_technical_reasoning: Most of this case is automatable, including 48-hour monitoring, but the specified physical power action and Task Manager visual check remain human setup/confirmation. They do not justify MANUAL ONLY because the core stress proceeds autonomously afterward.

source_provenance.history: Exact-code repository search including source script URL

no_automatic_retry: Do not resume, restart, extend or substitute the workload automatically after any interruption or safety stop. Preserve elapsed coverage and failure evidence.
